key_insight: With a fixed measurement basis, gate-optimal repetition-code tomography requires only 0, 1 and 5 recovery gates for 3, 5 and 7 qubits, respectively, and more correction is not always better.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing recovery rather than defaulting to minimum-weight decoding can reduce gate overhead and improve tomography precision on superconducting hardware.
method: Exhaustively enumerate recovery designs for 3-, 5- and 7-qubit repetition codes.
Determine rank using exact modular arithmetic at two primes.
Evaluate precision under a calibration-residual floor across sampled working points.
evidence_signal: At 40 sampled working points, the three-gate 3-qubit design was more precise than the standard six-gate decoder every time, with a median improvement of 9.5× and a range of 1.8–88×.
watch_item: Low recovery-gate counts do not guarantee practical tomography: conditioning keeps designs with 5 or more qubits out of reach in the reported analysis.
paper_title: Recovery gates as a resource in repetition-code process tomography: exhaustive gate-optimal designs for three, five and seven qubits
